title: Emend track-changes attribution record
description: One attribution record in `.emend/changes/<document-uuid>.json` (TD-4; `<document-uuid>` is the document's UUID from `.emend/docs.json`),keyed by `id` in the persisted file (`{"<change-id>": ChangeRecord, ...}`) — this schema validates one record's value. Track-changes is single-writer by design (only the author decides changes, D19): the file holds the *current* record set, so last-write-wins per id is correct by construction; there is no cross-author causal fold like `comment-event.schema.json`'s. The record deliberately carries no range/text of its own — the CriticMarkup marker live in the document is the source of truth for *what* changed (TD-2); this schema only records *who* changed it, how it's grouped/noted, and, once the author decides it, its `outcome`.

created_at.description: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch this change was first proposed.

updated_at.description: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch this record was last written — the single-writer last-write-wins tie-break (TD-4/D19).

group.description: Links this change to every other change decided together with it. Null is a singleton change.

change_set.description: The atomic `propose_changes` delivery this change belongs to (its returned `change_set_id`).

outcome.description: The change's recorded decision (FR-AGENT-9, TD-1 amendment #92): `accepted` or `rejected` once a saved document decides it, `null` while it is undecided, after an undo restores its marker, or while a save is replacing an earlier decision. Emend alone writes it, and only while saving the document: first `null` to every record whose value the save changes, then the document, then each decision that document implies, so a stored decision always describes the document on disk. An absent field means no save since this field existed has touched the record; only then may a reader fall back to a thread's linked-change decision. It states the outcome and nothing more. A live CriticMarkup marker that joins this record outranks it: the change is pending whatever this field says (TD-2). Additive and optional, so `schema_version` stays 1.

anchor.$comment: TD-4's shared anchor shape, as persisted in sidecar files (includes base_revision). Identical definition to `comment-event.schema.json`'s `$defs.anchor` — duplicated rather than cross-file $ref'd to keep each schema file self-contained (matches `provider-contract/mcp-tool-call.schema.json`'s convention).
